sections.heading: Telling a friend what to do
sections.body:
The affirmative *tú* command of regular verbs looks exactly like the *él / ella* present form: *hablar → habla*, *comer → come*, *escribir → escribe*. Stem changes stay: *cerrar → cierra*, *dormir → duerme*, *pedir → pide*.

*Habla más despacio.* (Speak more slowly.) *Come la sopa.* (Eat the soup.) *Escribe tu nombre aquí.* (Write your name here.)

Pronouns attach to the end, and an accent keeps the stress where it was: *Llámame* (Call me). *Dímelo* comes later. *Levántate* (Get up). *Siéntate* (Sit down).

sections.heading: Some irregular tú commands
sections.body:
A few very common verbs have short irregular commands: *ven* (come — from *venir*), *ten* (have / take — *tener*), *pon* (put — *poner*), *sal* (go out — *salir*), *haz* (do / make — *hacer*), *di* (say — *decir*), *ve* (go — *ir*), *sé* (be — *ser*). You'll practise these more in A2; for now, recognise *ven aquí* (come here) and *ten cuidado* (be careful).

For polite requests to strangers, a question is softer: *¿Me ayuda, por favor?* *¿Puede repetir?*

sections.heading: Asking for and giving directions
sections.body:
Ask: *Perdón, ¿dónde está la estación?* *¿Cómo llego al museo?* (How do I get to the museum?) *¿Está lejos?*

Give directions with commands: *Sigue derecho* (go straight — *todo recto* in Spain), *gira / dobla a la derecha* (turn right), *gira a la izquierda* (turn left), *cruza la calle* (cross the street), *toma la segunda calle* (take the second street). Then: *Está en la esquina* (on the corner), *está a dos cuadras* (two blocks away — *manzanas* in Spain).

examples: Excuse me, where is the station?
How do I get to the museum?
Gira a la derecha en el semáforo.
Turn right at the traffic light.
Toma la segunda calle a la derecha.
Take the second street on the right.
El banco está en la esquina.
The bank is on the corner.
Toma la primera calle a la izquierda.
Take the first street on the left.

exercises.answer: Toma la segunda calle a la derecha.
